linkedin.about: Steven Bartlett is a 33-year-old British entrepreneur, investor in more than 100 companies, speaker, author, and media owner. He is the founder of Steven.com - the creator media company. Through it's podcast creator "label" called FlightStory, they create and scales new media podcast IP and commercialise that IP through brand partnerships, programmatic revenue, events, book publishing, newsletters, e-commerce, and new product development. He is also the co-founder of thirdweb, a developer platform powering over 100,000 teams to build and launch web3 applications, and FlightCast, a video-first podcast hosting platform used by some of the world’s largest shows. Steven first gained recognition as the co-founder and CEO of Social Chain AG, a social media marketing and e-commerce company he launched at 21 and took public on a European stock exchange by the age of 27 via reverse merger. Social Chain AG became a globally recognised business with hundreds of employees across London, Manchester, Berlin, New York, and Los Angeles, working with major brands including Amazon, Apple, and Coca-Cola. Through his Fund and personal investments, he has backed companies including SpaceX, Huel, ZOE, Whoop, MrBeast, Groq, KetoneIQ, Cadence, PerfectTed, and over 60 others - focusing on businesses that improve human health, happiness, and performance. Steven is also the creator and host of The Diary of a CEO, currently the world's most downloaded / watched podcast and the fastest-growing podcast in the world. He is the youngest-ever investor on BBC’s Dragons’ Den. linkedin.activityText: Steven Bartlett Steven Bartlett 2h Steven Bartlett shared this He infiltrated criminal networks in Colombia because normal life was boring. This is Shawn Ryan. He joined the US Navy at 17, became a Navy SEAL, went on to work as a CIA contractor, and has since built one of the biggest podcasts in the world. When we sat down, I told Shawn that it feels like he has lived several different lives. And I don’t think I’ve ever meant that more literally. One of the most unexpected parts of his story is what happened to his faith. He told me about an experience where he believes he saw hell, describing it as complete emptiness, fear and the absence of God. For someone who has spent so much of his life around war, danger and intelligence, it was this experience that seemed to have changed him in a completely different way. And that is only one chapter of his life. We discussed things like: -⁠ ⁠Why he went to Colombia and embedded himself inside criminal networks. -⁠ ⁠Why he says he went to hell and came back seeing faith differently. - ⁠What he saw across Haiti, Afghanistan and Iraq that he still remembers today. - ⁠How podcasts could be used to manipulate millions of people. - ⁠Why politicians lying to his face changed how he sees politics. - ⁠Why he thinks China benefits every time America weakens itself. What makes Shawn’s perspective so interesting is that he hasn’t just studied these worlds from the outside. He has lived inside many of them. There were things in this conversation I probably would have dismissed several years ago. But doing this podcast has made me far more careful about assuming I understand what is possible. You don’t have to agree with everything Shawn believes. But his perspective is absolutely worth hearing. SOME NEWS 🚨 this year I’m joining @sharktankabc !!! 📺 🇺🇸 this was a dream of mine AND my mums...let me explain👇🏾

My nigerian mum raised 4 of us without being able to read or write herself, having left school when she was a child in Nigeria.

I struggled with school too - I wasn’t a smart kid and couldn’t pay attention, so I quickly realised the “traditional path” wasn’t going to work for someone like me

Then, when I was 12 years old, I discovered Dragons’ Den! 🐉

Me and my mum both fell in love with the show. Looking back, I think entrepreneurship offered us both hope - a path to a better life for people like us, who couldn’t pass tests in a classroom but were willing to work hard.

At 12 I would pause the TV and give my verdict, as if I was the 6th Dragon

By 16 I’d discovered Shark Tank and was starting my first (terrible) businesses

By 18 I was a university dropout with a start-up

And somehow, 9 years later, I ended up sitting in one of those Dragons’ Den chairs I used to shout at from our sofa

My mum has never fully gotten over it. 

When I call her today, 6 years later, the conversation is still 80% Dragons’ Den - her opinion on what I said, the businesses, what SHE would have done...

Btw, i’m genuinely not sure if she knows I have a podcast 😂 i don’t think she’s ever mentioned it 😅

But she knows Dragons’ Den, and that’s more than enough for her.

I know she’s always wanted me to do Shark Tank, so this phone call - telling her that day had come absolutely made my day, and hopefully her’s too!

I very much hope to do her proud + all of you that have supported me for the longest time... wish me luck!! 👊🏾❤️

P.S who would win in a fight, a shark 🦈 or a dragon 🐉 ???
